clue.text: Extremely crafty quintet brags about disreputable online activity

indicators.note: only the extremes of the next word are wanted: its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of crafty

indicators.note: about in the sense of round and round, so the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Five sly boasters chatter about some shady internet practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes CY from crafty; 'about' rearranges QUINTET BRAGS to give BERSQUATTING. Cybersquatting is registering a domain name that trades on someone else's trademark.
explanation.definitionFit: Grabbing web domains matching famous brand names in order to sell them back is a shady internet practice.

clue.text: Token for trial demo (a responsive one)

parts.note: a counter is a token used in games
pro = for, in favour of
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A token gesture laid on as a trial demonstration, one meant to answer something.
explanation.walkthrough: "Demo" is short for demonstration in the protest sense, not a trial product; the bracket narrows it to a protest made in reply to another.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterprotest is a demonstration staged in response to another one.

clue.text: Airline finally can advance, having secured one place for aircraft

indicators.note: the outer letters hold on to, or secure, the inner ones

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: the last letters of each of the two words that follow

parts.note: last letters of can and advance
I is the Roman numeral for one
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: An airline is finally allowed to expand after acquiring a site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' works on both of the next two words, not just can; 'having secured' then wraps the airline's letters round one and place.
explanation.definitionFit: A biplane is an early aeroplane with two pairs of wings, one stacked above the other.

clue.text: Large grounds are located all in the middle of the country

parts.note: middle letter of Large
middle letter of grounds
middle letter of are
middle letter of located
middle letter of all

explanation.surface: Big estates all sit at the centre of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the middle' takes the centre letter of each of the five words: R, U, R, A, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes the countryside, as opposed to towns and cities.

clue.text: Financial wizard covering a doctor's 25 per cent cut?

parts.note: a quant is a quantitative analyst in finance
as printed
DR = doctor

explanation.surface: A money whizz demanding a quarter share of a doctor's earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fee or commission; the definition is geometric, a quarter of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrant is a quarter of a circle, a 25 per cent slice.

clue.text: Reluctant explorers headed east

parts.note: CAVERS, cave explorers, minus the C
E = east

explanation.surface: Some unwilling explorers set off towards the east.
explanation.walkthrough: "Headed east" reads as a direction of travel; here "headed" means beheaded, and "east" simply adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be averse to something is to be unwilling to do it.

clue.text: Play electronic music, receiving cheer of approval

parts.note: trance is a genre of electronic dance music
olé, the Spanish cry of approval

explanation.surface: Someone playing a set of electronic music and getting cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: "Play" looks like a verb about the DJ; it is the noun, as in play in a steering wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is the permitted play or slack in a mechanism.

clue.text: Type of salt regularly in oil and stock

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so the letters are taken at a steady every-other spacing

parts.note: the even letters of iN oIl
stock as in a stock phrase: trite, hackneyed

explanation.surface: Kitchen talk: a salt used regularly in oil and in a stock.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stock" looks like soup base in the cooking surface; it is the adjective meaning hackneyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrite is a salt of nitrous acid, used for curing meat.

clue.text: Seat assignment sent out as text?

indicators.note: the letters are dispatched in a new order

parts.note: fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An airline sending a passenger's seat allocation by text message.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that an instant message is an example of a text rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant message is a short text sent and read in real time.

clue.text: Feature of US drug lawsuit?

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug
a case is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A drugs trial as a hallmark of American life.
explanation.walkthrough: "US" reads as the country; the definition means the two letters themselves, which are written as capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: capital letters are one thing the abbreviation for the United States always has.

clue.text: Admit to knowing head of local school

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front end, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of LOCAL
Eton is the famous English boarding school

explanation.surface: A local headteacher confessing to being in the know.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs "head" and "school" to suggest a headteacher, but "head of" only asks for one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is to reveal or admit that you know something.

clue.text: Follow Tesla alongside track

parts.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density
a rail is a track

explanation.surface: Driving behind a Tesla car along a road next to a railway.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car brand; here it is the scientific unit, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: trailing a suspect means shadowing them from behind.

clue.text: Control of retinue taken by others

indicators.note: something taken by a person is held in their grasp, so the retinue ends up inside the others

parts.note: the rest = the others
a train is a group of followers, a retinue

explanation.surface: Other people seizing command of a royal entourage.
explanation.walkthrough: "Retinue taken by others" puts the container second: the thing doing the taking is the outer word, even though it comes last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: showing restraint means keeping yourself in check.

clue.text: Wine periodically arrived with stronger, mixed drink

indicators.note: takes letters at regular intervals

parts.note: the even letters of aRrIvEd
a sling is a mixed drink of spirits such as gin, stronger than wine

explanation.surface: Someone who turned up now and then, bringing a harder cocktail as well as wine.
explanation.walkthrough: "Mixed" looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the description of the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white wine from the grape of that name.

clue.text: Artist's work wins top prize at the end

parts.note: to land a prize is to win it
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

indicators.note: takes the last letter of PRIZE

parts.note: the last letter of PRIZE

explanation.surface: A painter's canvas taking first prize at the final judging.
explanation.walkthrough: "Top prize" reads as one phrase; "top" gives CAP and only the end of "prize" is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting of scenery, an artist's work.

clue.text: An academic from Quito, say

parts.note: as printed
a dean is a senior academic

explanation.surface: A university lecturer who comes from the capital of Ecuador.
explanation.walkthrough: Quito, the capital of Ecuador, lies high in the Andes; "say" marks it as one example of an Andean place.
explanation.definitionFit: Andean means from the Andes, where Quito stands.

clue.text: Cats maybe cross over threshold?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns the letters over, bottom to top

parts.note: cats are an example of pets
a rood is a cross, a crucifix

explanation.surface: Cats wondering whether to cross the threshold into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cross over" looks like one phrasal verb; "cross" is the noun ROOD and "over" turns everything round.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstep is the step at a door, loosely its threshold.

clue.text: Sport thriving from just after its inception

indicators.note: starts the word one letter after its beginning, dropping the first

parts.note: growing = thriving

explanation.surface: A sport that flourished almost from the day it was founded.
explanation.walkthrough: The long phrase reads as history of the sport; it simply drops the G from GROWING.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: rowing is one sport among many, raced in boats with oars.

clue.text: I'm enjoying this story — it may well be full of rubbish

definitions.text: it may well be full of rubbish

parts.note: whee! is a cry of enjoyment
a story is a lie

explanation.surface: A reader loving a tale while admitting it is probably nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a wheelie, short for wheelie bin, is a wheeled household rubbish bin. "Full of rubbish" seems to judge the story, but it describes the bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelie bin is where household rubbish goes.

clue.text: Drive in second? Er …

parts.note: a second is a moment
um and er are both sounds of hesitation

explanation.surface: A learner driver asking whether to drive in second gear, then hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: "Drive in second" suggests gears, but "in" is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a campaign with momentum has drive, the push that keeps it moving forward.

clue.text: Visitor to Oz touring river close to city

parts.note: Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz
R = river
on = close to, as in a town on the coast

explanation.surface: A tourist in Australia going round a river near a city.
explanation.walkthrough: "Oz" reads as slang for Australia; the visitor is Dorothy's dog in the land of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Canada's largest city stands for cities in general.

clue.text: Spirit of good admin worker broken by criticism

parts.note: G = good
PA = personal assistant
a rap is a rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A good office assistant whose morale is crushed by criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: "Spirit" reads as morale; it is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian spirit distilled from grape residue.

clue.text: Money manager less hesitant after rate changes

indicators.note: the comparative comes after the reworked word
the word rate changes its form, its letters reordered

parts.note: surer means more certain, so less hesitant

explanation.surface: A finance officer grows more confident once the interest rate moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less hesitant' needs a comparative, more sure; 'changes' acts on rate alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer looks after the funds of a club, company or society.

clue.text: People working together in part of Apple broadcast?

indicators.note: says it out loud, over the air

parts.note: the core is the centre of an apple

explanation.surface: A team collaborating in a division of the tech company Apple, on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A pushes towards the company; the fruit is meant. CORPS is said "core", with silent P and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is a body of people working together, like a press corps.

clue.text: Smoke starts to intoxicate gamblers inside saloon, perhaps

indicators.note: the opening letters go within the vehicle

parts.note: a saloon is a type of car, the British name for a sedan

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words that follow

parts.note: first letters of intoxicate and gamblers

explanation.surface: In a Wild West saloon, smoke and drink go to the gamblers' heads.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a Western bar, but saloon here is the British word for a sedan, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example of the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar is a roll of tobacco leaves for smoking, and a smoke is a common informal name for one.

clue.text: Series of coordinated steps featuring in appraisals, annoyingly

indicators.note: the answer appears inside the following words

parts.note: the run starts near the end of the first word and crosses the comma into the second

explanation.surface: A tiresome step-by-step process that keeps turning up in staff reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like office procedure; the steps are dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: any dance is a sequence of steps moved in time, and this Latin one is the example.

clue.text: Father travelling again to region of South America

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: letters that travel move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad sets off on his journeys once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling' looks like part of the father's story, but it signals that 'again to' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia is the southern tip of the continent, shared between Argentina and Chile.

clue.text: Open super-large complex useful for many things

indicators.note: the letters are tangled into a new arrangement

parts.note: fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A huge new complex opening its doors, built to serve many uses.
explanation.walkthrough: "Complex" reads as a noun, a building; it is the adjective telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something general-purpose is useful for many different jobs.
